security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation false positives from Markdown backticks, Vaex memory-mapping terms, and data-analysis vocabulary. Confirmed risks are limited to insecure remote-server guidance and credential-handling examples. No evidence found of prompt injection, malware behavior, or automatic command execution.

remediation.suggestion: Default server examples to localhost, add auth and TLS guidance, and warn before binding to 0.0.0.0.
Use environment-managed credentials, cloud IAM roles, profiles, or secret managers instead of key literals and credential JSON examples.

remediation.issue: External service promotion in runtime instructions
remediation.suggestion: Remove the K-Dense Web upsell from runtime instructions, or move neutral ownership details to documentation.

content.value_statement: Large tabular datasets often exceed local memory and make pandas workflows slow. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Vaex workflows for lazy analysis, conversion, visualization, and ML.
actual_capabilities: Open HDF5, Arrow, Parquet, CSV, and FITS data using Vaex patterns.
Convert large CSV files to HDF5 for faster repeated loading.
Create virtual columns, filters, selections, groupby aggregations, and binned statistics.
Build heatmaps, histograms, scatter plots, and selection-based visualizations.
Apply Vaex performance patterns such as lazy evaluation, delay batching, caching, and materialization.
Reference Vaex ML workflows with encoders, scaling, PCA, clustering, and model integrations.
limitations: Requires the Vaex Python library and matching optional I/O dependencies.
Does not validate the contents, licenses, or permissions of user datasets.
Remote server and cloud storage examples need secure deployment choices by the user.
Some Vaex APIs may differ across installed package versions.

use_cases.title: Explore Billion-Row Tables
use_cases.description: Profile, filter, and aggregate large local datasets without loading every row into memory.

use_cases.title: Modernize CSV Pipelines
use_cases.description: Convert slow CSV exports into HDF5 or Arrow workflows with reusable checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Visualize Scientific Data
use_cases.description: Create aggregate plots and summaries for astronomical, financial, or sensor datasets.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Large File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Vaex to inspect my large dataset. Recommend the best file format, loading method, and first summary checks.

prompt_templates.title: Convert CSV Efficiently
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Vaex workflow that converts a large CSV to HDF5, validates columns, and keeps repeat analysis fast.

prompt_templates.title: Build Aggregations and Plots
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Vaex aggregations and visualizations for these columns, using lazy expressions and selections where useful.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Production Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Vaex pipeline for memory use, delayed execution, materialization, caching, checkpointing, and secure remote data access.

output_examples.input: Help me convert a 40 GB CSV to a reusable format.
output_examples.output: A staged plan recommending Vaex CSV conversion, HDF5 export, column validation, timing checks, and safe source-file retention.

output_examples.input: I need fast summaries by region and product.
output_examples.output: A Vaex aggregation strategy using virtual columns, groupby summaries, delayed execution, and checks for missing data.

output_examples.input: My scatter plot is too slow for millions of rows.
output_examples.output: A visualization approach using binned Vaex plots, percentile limits, sensible grid shapes, and cached aggregations.

best_practices: Convert repeated large CSV workflows to HDF5 or Arrow before deep analysis.
Keep transformations lazy with virtual columns until materialization is clearly needed.
Protect cloud credentials and remote Vaex servers before sharing examples or commands.
anti_patterns: Do not convert massive Vaex datasets to pandas unless memory capacity is verified.
Do not bind remote data servers to public interfaces without access controls.
Do not hardcode cloud keys or commit credential files in analysis projects.

faq.question: What is Vaex best for?
faq.answer: Vaex is best for lazy analysis, aggregation, and visualization of tabular data larger than memory.

faq.question: Does this skill install Vaex?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for environments where Vaex and needed dependencies are installed.

faq.question: Can it replace pandas?
faq.answer: It helps when pandas workflows exceed memory. Pandas may still fit smaller, fully in-memory tasks.

faq.question: Which file formats are recommended?
faq.answer: HDF5 and Arrow are preferred for repeated Vaex work. Parquet is useful for distributed data systems.

faq.question: Can it help with visualization?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers binned plots, heatmaps, histograms, selections, and publication-oriented visualization choices.

faq.question: Can it handle cloud data?
faq.answer: Yes, with optional storage libraries. Users must configure credentials and remote access securely.
